request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Date of Admission: [INSERT DATE]
Date of Discharge: [INSERT DATE]

Patient Name: [INSERT NAME]                    MR#[INSERT MR NUMBER]
Clinical Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Medical History:
The patient had chronic renal failure, hypertension, and a history of smoking and morbid obesity.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the emergency department with exertional dyspnea, shortness of breath, and recurrent episodes of acute pulmonary edema. Upon physical examination, he had bilateral pulmonary rales, lower extremities edema, and a large pulsative mass that was noticed during abdominal examination. Emergency CT scans revealed an infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) of 9.8 cm size with communication between the aorta and the IVC without any signs of a retroperitoneal rupture. 

Treatment:
The patient underwent an emergency laparotomy and aortic cross-clamping, during which a 20 × 15 mm aortocaval communication was discovered after opening the aortic sac. The bleeding from the IVC was controlled by digital compression, and the fistula was oversawn from within the sac with monofilament sutures. After that, a 20mm Dacron tube graft was placed to restore perfusion.

Post-Surgical Management:
The patient was shifted to the ICU after surgery and received continuous venovenous haemofiltration due to acute renal failure, which resolved on the fourth postoperative day. The patient was extubated on the tenth postoperative day and discharged after 25 days of hospitalization. At discharge, he exhibited bilateral peripheral edema but no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. His edemas' have resolved, and the patient remains in good health 16 months after the operation.

Follow-up Care:
The patient's follow-up appointments for the surgical site have been scheduled. The clinical team will monitor and manage related medical symptoms and tackle his pre-existing conditions appropriately.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: I71**

The principal diagnosis is the infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (9.8 cm), which was the reason for emergency admission and surgery. It falls under chapter I (circulatory system) and category I71 (aortic aneurysm and dissection). The aortocaval fistula is a complication of the aneurysm, and the renal failure, pulmonary oedema and obesity are comorbidities.
